newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends barely changed, rangebound.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends barely changed, rangebound.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended another day barely changed as speculative selling and trade scale-down buying confined prices to a narrow trading range, dealers said.
The benchmark May contract settled 0.01 cent weaker at 10.76 cents a lb, having ranged from 10.81 to 10.69. The back months closed 0.01 higher to 0.05 cent lower.
Volume was estimated to have reached 20,887 lots compared with the official 18,487 lots Wednesday.

Floor sources said the market remained on the defensive for most of the day with the speculators cited as early sellers. Unable to trigger sell stops around 10.68 cents, some of the speculators covered short positions later in the day.
One floor source said noted recent lows of 10.69, 10.67 and now 10.69, on the weekly chart, forming a support level.
Contributing support was steady scale-down buying by the trade from the mid-10.70-cent area.
"The trade absorbed a lot of spec liquidation," a dealer said, noting trade buying around 20 points in the May/July spread.
He said prices could hold above support in the near term. "The trade needs to buy back short positions and they're not willing to wait that long to do so," he added.
Other industry sources expect the market to succumb to pressure if prices fail to garner momentum to the upide over the next few sessions.
Resistance was not noted until the recent high of 11.09 basis May, while support below 10.68 cents was pegged at 10.50 cents.
